sections.h2: Where is Berkeley County, West Virginia?
sections.html:
Berkeley County is in the Shenandoah Valley, in the Eastern Panhandle of West Virginia, with Martinsburg as the county seat. It is part of the Hagerstown-Martinsburg metropolitan area and covers 321.56 square miles.

The county was founded on May 15, 1772, and it is the second most populous of West Virginia's 55 counties, behind Kanawha County. The 2020 census counted 122,076 residents, and the 2025 estimate cited by Wikipedia is 139,522. Within the county are the city of Martinsburg, the town of Hedgesville and the census-designated places of Falling Waters and Inwood.

Berkeley County has six magisterial districts: Adam Stephens, Norborne, Potomac, Shenandoah, Tuscarora and Valley. Jefferson County was formed from its eastern section on January 8, 1801.

sections.h2: What is the history of Martinsburg and Berkeley County?
sections.html:
Martinsburg mattered to both armies in the Civil War because the main line of the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad ran through it. Control of the town changed hands many times, especially before the Battle of Gettysburg in July 1863, and afterward it stayed mostly under Union control.

Berkeley and Jefferson counties voted in 1863 to join West Virginia. Virginia sued, and in 1871 the U.S. Supreme Court decided Virginia v. West Virginia and upheld the transfer. The railroad shops that gave the town its industrial base are now listed as the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad Martinsburg Shops, and other historic sites include the Adam Stephen House and the Hedgesville Historic District.

Historic districts and older houses can mean extra care in a sale. If your house is old, ask the city or county whether any local historic designation applies before you plan exterior changes or a teardown.

The homeowners association group matters if your house is in a community with an HOA. Before closing, ask the association for a payoff or a statement of unpaid dues, since a buyer or title company will want to know about any balance.

sections.h2: How is Berkeley County property assessed under West Virginia law?
sections.html:
The county assessor values property, and the sheriff bills and collects the tax. As of July 1 each year, ownership, use and value are set for the next calendar tax year. The State Tax Division says county boards of education, county commissions, municipalities and the State all levy property tax.

The state constitution creates four property classes:

  • Class I: intangible personal property and certain farm personal property, with nothing currently taxed.
  • Class II: owner-occupied homes used only as a residence, and farmland used for agriculture.
  • Class III: property outside a municipality not in Class I or II.
  • Class IV: property inside a municipality not in Class I or II.

An investor who buys your owner-occupied house and rents it moves it out of Class II, so the tax can change after the sale.

sections.h2: When can you protest a Berkeley County assessment?
sections.html:
You protest to the county commission sitting as the board of equalization and review. That board begins meeting on February 1 each year and must adjourn by February 28, and your protest must be filed before that year's taxes are due.

  • Gather evidence of value, such as an independent appraisal or repair estimates.
  • Check the county assessor's record for errors in square footage, bedrooms or condition.
  • Ask the assessor's office how to file with the commission, at 400 West Stephen Street, Suite 106, Martinsburg.
  • If the dispute is about classification or taxability, the question can go to the Tax Commissioner under West Virginia Code 11-3-24a, with a ruling due by the end of February.

The state also publishes the dates on which it sends notices when an assessed value rises. If you are selling, an increase in the assessed value can change the tax a buyer will inherit, so check the notice before you close.

sections.h2: What deadlines apply to property tax and the homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Tax tickets are issued on or after July 15. The first installment is due September 1 and the second March 1. A discount applies if you pay before each of those dates, and interest accrues once a half becomes delinquent on October 1 or April 1.

The homestead exemption deadline is December 1. Under West Virginia Code 11-6B-3, the first $20,000 of assessed value of a homestead is exempt when the owner is 65 or older, or certified permanently and totally disabled, and has lived in West Virginia for the two consecutive calendar years before the tax year. An owner who receives a similar exemption in another state cannot also claim this one.

Berkeley County residents can call the Sheriff's Tax Office at (304) 264-1982 for a balance. The County Assessor's number listed by the county is 304-264-1904. Confirm details with the office before you rely on a date.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Berkeley County?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Berkeley County follows the usual West Virginia closing steps with no mortgage on the buyer's side. You describe the house, receive a written offer and decide. An attorney or title company records the deed, pays off liens and settles tax.

sections.h2: What do Berkeley County sellers commonly face?
sections.html:
• Inherited houses with heirs spread across several states.
  • Properties in a homeowners association with unpaid dues.
  • Rentals the owner no longer wants to manage.
  • Owners who are behind on a tax installment and want to avoid interest.

For each one, a first step helps. Get the HOA balance in writing, get the tax balance from the Sheriff's Tax Office, and collect the death certificate and court papers for an inherited house. This page is general information and is not legal or tax advice, so confirm details with the county office or a licensed professional.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to protest a Berkeley County assessment?
faqs.a: The county commission sits as the board of equalization and review from February 1 and must adjourn by February 28. File before that year's taxes are due.

faqs.q: When are Berkeley County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Tickets are issued on or after July 15. The first installment is due September 1 and the second March 1, and each half becomes delinquent on October 1 and April 1.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for the $20,000 homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Owners 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, who occupy the home and meet the two-year West Virginia residency rule. The application deadline is December 1.
It covers 321.56 square miles, and its 2020 population was 122,076, which makes it the second most populous county in West Virginia.

faqs.q: Will my property tax change if the buyer rents the house?
faqs.a: It can. Owner-occupied residential property is Class II, and a rented house falls in Class III or Class IV depending on whether it is inside a municipality.
